title: SAML session TTL harmonization and admin step-up / JIT session binding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customer-facing SAML integrations observe inconsistent session behavior across IdPs and Redwood (SP). Sessions sometimes outlive IdP assertions or are unexpectedly invalidated after JIT provisioning. Admin/privileged actions lack explicit step-up/reauth semantics tied to SAML session attributes, and logout/IdP-initiated SLO flows are not reliably reflected in audit logs. This ticket defines a cross-cutting solution: align session TTLs with IdP metadata where possible, introduce a session-binding token for JIT-provisioned accounts to preserve continuity without extending implicit trust, and add explicit step-up hooks for admin-sensitive routes that trigger re-auth or MFA depending on SAML assertions and RBAC v2 elevation paths. The scope includes runtime changes, console UX flags for admin controls, audit logging schema updates, and a phased rollout with canary metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Sessions created via SAML respect IdP session TTL when IdP exposes SessionNotOnOrAfter / SessionIndex; when not present, Redwood applies conservative TTL policy configurable per-tenant

JIT-provisioned accounts receive a short-lived session-binding token (SB-<hex>) recorded in audit logs; SB token persists across immediate account provisioning flows to avoid double-login but is invalidated on rebind/revoke

Admin-sensitive endpoints (role changes, API key creation, billing, workspace export) enforce step-up: either IdP re-auth challenge or Redwood MFA (per customer preference) before completing the action
SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout flows clear session state and emit an audit event with fields: session_id, sb_token, logout_initiator, timestamp, outcome
No increase in median end-user login latency > 50ms for SAML flows after changes
Automated test coverage for SAML session TTL parsing, SB token lifecycle, and logout/event emission added to integration suite
Documentation (Console settings, API changes, and admin UX) updated and linked in the PR
notes: Design tradeoffs: aligning TTLs tightly with IdP reduces stale sessions but may shorten UX; default will be conservative (30m) unless IdP asserts longer TTL and tenant opts in
SB token is ephemeral (default 15m) and is scoped to the session window when account is created via JIT to avoid friction for first-run workflows
We will not trust arbitrary IdP attributes for RBAC elevation without explicit mapping and verification; RBAC v2 role grants must pass a mapping policy and, where required, trigger step-up
Audit schema change: add 'sb_token' and 'logout_initiator' string fields; existing tools consuming logs must be updated (observability/ingest team notified)
implementation_steps: Add SAML assertion parsing enhancements to extract SessionNotOnOrAfter and SessionIndex; unit tests for known IdP variants (Okta, AzureAD, GoogleWorkspace)
Introduce SB token generator and storage in session store (Redis) with TTL and single-use rebind semantics
Implement step-up middleware for admin routes that consults tenant policy: preferred_reauth_source = {idp, redwood-mfa}
Wire logout flows: SP-initiated SLO should call IdP SLO endpoint when available; both flows write audit event via new log schema
Add Console flag 'Enforce IdP TTL' per-tenant and admin UI to configure step-up preference
Update e2e tests and integration harness; add load tests for SAML login peak QPS to validate latency impact
Draft migration runbook and rollback path (disable 'Enforce IdP TTL' flag and revert step-up middleware if issues)
